title: Railless navigation exploration notes
content:
Context / goal:
This note collects early exploration ideas for a non-rail (railless) console navigation approach intended to reduce cognitive load for teams with many routes (models, deployments, routes, observability panels) while keeping fast access to common actions. Background: current left-rail has grown vertically, pushing lower-priority pages off-screen and introducing long scanning times. We need alternatives that preserve discoverability for admin areas while surfacing frequent tasks for engineers.

What we mean by railless navigation (rough):
- Replace a dense, tall left rail with a compact, multi-mode header + context-aware micro-hub that expands inline.
- Primary affordance: a small persistent top bar with: global search, primary area selector (Host / Dedicated / Private), and a contextual micro-hub button that expands to show area-specific routes and quick actions.
- Secondary affordance: page-level breadcrumbs + a sticky mini-TOC for deep pages (traces, logs, token breakdown).

Principles / constraints:
- Keep route names short and action-focused (e.g., "Routes" vs "Route configuration").
- No more than 6 top-level buckets visible by default to avoid excessive scanning.
- Support muscle-memory: keyboard-first flows (cmd-k to jump, alt-1..6 to switch global areas).
- Preserve tenant isolation: for Private deployments we show only allowed routes; the micro-hub should be able to be governed by role checks at render time.
- Accessibility: ensure expanded micro-hub is announced, focus trap while open, color contrast >= 4.5:1.

Exploration sketches (textual wireframes):
1) Topbar + micro-hub (default compact)
   - Topbar: left: product logo (collapsible), center: area selector pill (Host · Dedicated · Private), right: global search, notifications, user menu.
   - Micro-hub button sits left of area selector, icon-only by default. On click, a panel anchors under topbar — left column: primary routes for selected area (2-6 items), right column: quick actions + recent items (open routes, recent evals).
   - Panel actions inline: New Route, Upload Model, Start Canary, View SLA.

2) Contextual page variants
   - When user lands on a model page, micro-hub shows model-related routes (versions, quantization, perf tests).
   - On the Observability pages the hub shows filters, pre-saved queries, and a one-click open in tracing view.

3) Compact persistent breadcrumb + mini-TOC
   - Under the topbar, show compact breadcrumb that includes a small chevron menu; open that chevron to quickly navigate sibling pages without leaving the current context.
   - The mini-TOC pins to the right edge on wide screens and slides in on mobile.

Route condensation heuristics (how we decide what to show in hub):
- Frequency-first: surface pages with >100 visits in last 30 days per org (configurable).
- Role-weighted: admin-only pages hidden for non-admins in the default collapsed view but discoverable via "all routes" link.
- Recency boost: recently visited pages appear in "recent" area even if below frequency threshold.
- Cost-sensitivity: routes with high-cost per token (e.g., batch eval infra) get a secondary badge in hub to increase discoverability of cost controls.

Backlog grooming items (candidate tickets):
- RED-1387: micro-hub component — skeleton + ARIA semantics (owner: Jordan) (spike: 3d)
- RED-1420: topbar area selector & keyboard shortcuts (owner: Avery) (spike: 2d)
- RED-1499: condensed route-ranking pipeline (backend + UI) (owner: Ravi) (sprint 23)
- RED-1502: mini-TOC accessibility and mobile slide-in behavior (owner: Lina)

Unresolved UX decisions / risks:
- Deep linking: how do we encode hub state in URL? Option A: treat micro-hub as ephemeral state (no URL). Option B: push hub-state query param so shared links reconstruct hub content. Tradeoffs: ephemeral is simpler; param enables reproducible shared views and A/B tests.
- Discoverability for infrequent but critical pages (billing, audits). We need an "always-visible" affordance for critical admin pages whether or not condensed heuristics hide them.
- Migration for large customers: removing the left rail may break muscle memory. Consider an opt-in toggle + a one-month rollout where both rails exist and we collect usage telemetry.

Proposed migration plan (high-level):
- Phase 0: build micro-hub experimental component behind feature flag (internal-only).
- Phase 1: test with internal teams (SRE, Solutions Eng, Customer Success) for 2–3 weeks; capture task completion time for 5 core flows.
- Phase 2: gated alpha for 10 external customers (combo of Host, Dedicated, Private) with opt-in UI.
- Phase 3: gradual beta with default off for all orgs but enabled for new orgs.

Metrics we will monitor (signal we care about):
- Time-to-first-action for 5 canonical tasks (create-route, open-model-version, start-canary, open-traces, update-quota).
- Click depth: median number of clicks to reach target pages; expect drop from current baseline (rail) of ~2.1 -> target <=1.6.
- Feature adoption: % of active users who use micro-hub weekly.
- Support contact rate for "where is X" (measure via tagged CS tickets).
- Keyboard-first metrics: % of users using cmd-k or numeric shortcuts after 1 week.

Wireframe notes / micro-interactions to prototype: 
- Hub open animation: fade + slide down (150ms), focus lands on first actionable item.
- Empty-state hub: for new orgs show "Quickstarts" + video + create-first-route CTA.
- Long lists: if area has many routes, hub shows top items + an inline search with fuzzy match.
- Mobile: topbar collapses to icon row; micro-hub becomes a full-screen sheet with swipe-down to dismiss.

Accessibility checklist (pre-launch):
- ARIA roles for hub, proper aria-expanded on the button, keyboard order tested with screen readers.
- Color token audit for contrast.
- Ensure non-mouse interactions (arrow keys within hub, esc to close).

Open questions for next design sync (agenda):
1) Agree on what constitutes a "top-level bucket" and whether "Optimize" belongs in the main area selector or as a secondary hub item.
2) Decision on URL encoding for hub state and deep links.
3) Offline/slow network fallbacks: prefer skeleton loaders vs. progressive reveal?
4) Telemetry plan: what events we log for hub impressions, action clicks, and keyboard shortcuts?

Next steps (short term):
- Jordan: prototype micro-hub skeleton + ARIA semantics (deliverable: interactive Figma frames, due 2025-02-20).
- Avery: draft keyboard map and hotkey discoverability flow (deliverable: doc + example flows, due 2025-02-18).
- Ravi: spike on condensed route-ranking backend (deliverable: proto algorithm + test dataset, due 2025-02-24).
- Lina: write mobile slide-in interaction spec and accessibility test plan (deliverable: checklist + mobile frames, due 2025-02-22).

Notes to self: keep this exploration intentionally broad. We should aim for a lightweight alpha that validates faster task completion and reduced scanning; don’t try to solve everything (billing, org settings) in v1. Collect qualitative feedback early — watching 5 users navigate will catch 80% of painful assumptions.

References / inspirations:
- Figma frames: console/nav-explorations-2025 (internal)
- Google Cloud Console ideas (compact topbar patterns)
- Notion / Linear quick-switch flows (cmd-k discoverability)

End of note.
